title: Doe maar! — de gebiedende wijs
summary: Commands from the verb stem, and how even/maar/nou/eens soften them from bossy to friendly

blocks.title: Making a command
blocks.body: The imperative is the easiest form in Dutch: take the *ik*-form (the bare stem) and stop. **No ending, no pronoun.** *ik wacht* → **wacht!**, *ik kom* → **kom!**, *ik doe* → **doe!** Separable verbs still split, but here they just… don't: *ga zitten* (sit down), *let op* (watch out).

blocks.title: The one new thing: softeners
blocks.body: A bare command sounds *bossy*. Dutch fixes this with a tiny particle right after the verb. **even** = 'just / for a sec' (*Wacht even!*). **maar** = reassuring, 'go ahead' (*Kom maar binnen*). **eens** = inviting, 'have a…' (*Kijk eens*). **nou** = 'come on now'. These turn an order into an offer — this is the whole trick of sounding Dutch and kind.
blocks.callout: *Wacht!* barks. *Wacht even!* smiles. Same word, one particle.

blocks.title: Tap to hear the everyday commands

pairs.note: *even* turns an urgent bark into a friendly 'hang on a sec'.
*maar* reassures — 'come on over, it's fine, no pressure'.
*eens* makes it an invitation — 'take a look at this'.

blocks.prompt: A nervous friend is hovering in your doorway. Which sounds warm, not bossy?
blocks.explain: *Kom maar binnen* = 'come on in, it's fine'. The bare *Binnen!* is a command to a dog; the third is an obligation, not a welcome.

blocks.prompt: Turn *wachten* into a friendly 'Wait a second!' — verb plus one softener.
blocks.explain: *Wacht even!* — the stem *wacht* plus *even* ('for a sec') is the everyday version.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the friendly command.

blocks.scene: Emma is teaching You to make stamppot in her kitchen in de Pijp.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.target: Kom, we maken vanavond stamppot. Pak even een grote pan.
lines.en: Come on, we're making stamppot tonight. Grab a big pan for me.
lines.spotlight: Pak even — 'even' makes 'grab' a request, not an order.

lines.speaker: You
lines.en: Like this? And how much water?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.target: Doe maar flink wat erin. En snijd de boerenkool klein.
lines.en: Go ahead and put plenty in. And chop the kale small.
lines.spotlight: Doe maar — the friendliest command Dutch has.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.target: Let op je vingers, joh. Rustig.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.spotlight: Proef eens — 'eens' softens it into a warm invitation.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Mmm, lekker. Doe maar een snufje.
lines.en: Mmm, tasty. Go ahead, a pinch.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.en: Exactly. Come on, to the table!

questions.q: Wat moet You met de boerenkool doen?
Waarom zegt Emma 'let op je vingers'?

blocks.title: Build a friendly command
blocks.prompt: Assemble a warm, softened command a host might say.
Schrijf drie vriendelijke opdrachten die je een gast bij jou thuis zou geven. Gebruik minstens twee keer een verzachter (*even*, *maar*, *eens* of *nou*).
